---
title: "Environment Variables"
subtitle: "What you may change, and what changing it costs"
---

Every knob below is read from the environment at run time. They exist so a
researcher can explore the space around a contract, not so a result can be
tuned into passing.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two categories, and the difference matters

**Execution settings** change *how* a workload runs without changing what it
claims. Seed, device, and data location are in this group. A `max` result
produced with a different device is still a `max` result.

**Contract overrides** change *what the workload measures*. Epochs, batch
sizes, sequence lengths, iteration counts, and quality targets are in this
group. A run with any of these set is a research variant, not a comparable
`max` result, and the report records the override so a reviewer can see it.

If you are producing a result someone else will compare against, set nothing in
the second group.
:::

## Execution Settings

These are safe to set for a comparable run.

| **Variable** | **Meaning** | **Default** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `MLPERF_EDU_SEED` | Seed for every stochastic path in the run | `42` |
| `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_SEED` | Seed override consulted before `MLPERF_EDU_SEED` | unset |
| `MLPERF_EDU_DEVICE` | Force a torch device (`cpu`, `mps`, `cuda`) | auto-selected |
| `MLPERF_EDU_DATA_DIR` | Where fetched datasets and checkpoints live | project cache |
| `MLPERF_EDU_QUIET` | Set to `1` to silence per-epoch training progress | unset |
| `MLPERF_EDU_NO_BROWSER` | Set to `1` to stop reports opening a browser | unset |
| `MLPERF_EDU_HF_LOCAL_ONLY` | Set to `1` to forbid Hugging Face network access | unset |

Training runs report epoch, metric, elapsed time, and an estimate of time
remaining to stderr. `MLPERF_EDU_QUIET=1` turns that off; it never affects the
measured result.

## Contract Overrides

Setting any of these makes the run a research variant. They are grouped by the
workload they affect.

| **Workload** | **Variables** |
|:---|:---|
| recommendation | `MLPERF_EDU_NCF_MAX_EPOCHS`, `MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LEARNING_RATE`, `MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LR_SCHEDULE` |
| reinforcement learning | `MLPERF_EDU_MINIGO_GAMES_PER_GENERATION`, `MLPERF_EDU_MINIGO_GENERATIONS` |
| time-series forecasting | `MLPERF_EDU_TIMESERIES_MAX_EPOCHS`, `MLPERF_EDU_TIMESERIES_PATIENCE`, `MLPERF_EDU_TIMESERIES_HORIZON`, `MLPERF_EDU_TIMESERIES_MAX_TRAIN_BATCHES`, `MLPERF_EDU_TIMESERIES_MAX_EVAL_BATCHES`, `MLPERF_EDU_TIMESERIES_WORKERS` |
| graph node classification | `MLPERF_EDU_GRAPH_MAX_EPOCHS`, `MLPERF_EDU_GRAPH_MAX_LAYERS`, `MLPERF_EDU_GRAPH_MAX_HIDDEN_CHANNELS`, `MLPERF_EDU_GRAPH_MAX_LR`, `MLPERF_EDU_GRAPH_MAX_DROPOUT` |
| causal language modeling (training) | `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_ITERS`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_LR`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_MIN_LR`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_BETA2`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_SEQ_LEN`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_MODEL_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_WARMUP_ITERS`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_EVAL_INTERVAL`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_EVAL_ITERS`, `MLPERF_EDU_MAX_QUALITY_TARGET` |
| causal language modeling (prefill) | `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MIN_BATCH`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MIN_CONTEXT`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MIN_ITER`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MIN_WARMUP`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MAX_BATCH`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MAX_CONTEXT`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MAX_ITER`, `MLPERF_EDU_PREFILL_MAX_WARMUP` |
| causal language modeling (decode) | `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MIN_BATCH`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MIN_PREFILL_CTX`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MIN_STEPS`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MAX_BATCH`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MAX_PREFILL_CTX`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MAX_STEPS`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MAX_REPETITIONS`, `MLPERF_EDU_DECODE_MAX_WARMUPS` |
| image classification | `MLPERF_EDU_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION_MAX_REPETITIONS` |
| keyword spotting | `MLPERF_EDU_KEYWORD_SPOTTING_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_KEYWORD_SPOTTING_MAX_REPETITIONS`, `MLPERF_EDU_KEYWORD_SPOTTING_MAX_WARMUP_REPETITIONS` |
| visual wake words | `MLPERF_EDU_VISUAL_WAKE_WORDS_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_VISUAL_WAKE_WORDS_MAX_REPETITIONS`, `MLPERF_EDU_VISUAL_WAKE_WORDS_MAX_WARMUP_REPETITIONS` |
| anomaly detection | `MLPERF_EDU_ANOMALY_DETECTION_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_ANOMALY_DETECTION_MAX_REPETITIONS`, `MLPERF_EDU_ANOMALY_DETECTION_MAX_WARMUP_REPETITIONS` |
| text classification | `MLPERF_EDU_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MLPERF_EDU_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION_MAX_LENGTH`, `MLPERF_EDU_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION_MAX_REPETITIONS` |
| information retrieval | `MLPERF_EDU_RETRIEVAL_BATCH_SIZE` |
| image generation | `MLPERF_EDU_EDM_BATCH_SIZE` |
| code generation | `MLPERF_EDU_EVALPLUS_WORKERS` |

`MLPERF_EDU_MAX_QUALITY_TARGET` deserves specific mention. It replaces the
inherited quality target for causal language modeling. Lowering a target is the
exact move the suite exists to prevent, so a run that sets it can never be
score-bearing.

`MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LEARNING_RATE` and `MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LR_SCHEDULE` exist for one
open question. The recommendation contract fixes Adam at a constant rate, HR@10
peaks early and then declines, and the upstream reference may anneal instead.
Testing that requires varying the schedule without editing the contract, which
is what the `pro` envelope is for. `MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LR_SCHEDULE` accepts
`constant` (the contract behaviour and the default), `cosine`, or `step`. Both
variables reject malformed or non-positive values rather than falling back to
the contract, because an override that silently does nothing would make an
ablation look like a null result. Leaving both unset reproduces the canonical
`max` path exactly.

## Profile Controls

| **Variable** | **Meaning** |
|:---|:---|
| `MLPERF_EDU_PRO_REPETITIONS` | Repetition count for the `pro` research envelope |

## Asset and Handoff Controls

These point the runner at material you supply yourself, usually because a
license or a legacy runtime prevents the suite from fetching it.

| **Variable** | **Meaning** |
|:---|:---|
| `MLPERF_EDU_BFCL_IMPORT_PACKET` | Import a completed BFCL function-calling result |
| `MLPERF_EDU_EDM_IMPORT_PACKET` | Import a completed EDM image-generation result |
| `MLPERF_EDU_NANOGPT_CHECKPOINT` | Reuse a nanoGPT checkpoint instead of training |
| `MLPERF_EDU_NANOGPT_TRAIN_MANIFEST` | Provenance manifest for a reused checkpoint |
| `MLPERF_EDU_NANOGPT_TRAIN_REPORT` | Training report for a reused checkpoint |
| `MLPERF_EDU_MINIGO_IMAGE` | Container image digest for the MiniGo handoff |
| `MLPERF_EDU_MINIGO_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` | Container runtime for the MiniGo handoff |
| `MLPERF_EDU_MINIGO_PRO_GAMES_REVIEWED` | Reviewed game count for the MiniGo `pro` gate |
| `MLPERF_EDU_LAST_SIDECAR` | Internal: path to the most recent measurement sidecar |

## Retired Controls

These are read by code retained for the superseded DLRM contract. Recommendation
now inherits the MLPerf Training v0.5 NCF contract on MovieLens-20M and does not
consult them.

`MLPERF_EDU_CRITEO_TERMS_ACCEPTED`, `MLPERF_EDU_DLRM_DATA_DIR`,
`MLPERF_EDU_DLRM_CHECKPOINT`, `MLPERF_EDU_DLRM_DEVICE`, `MLPERF_EDU_DLRM_PYTHON`.
